newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHARE TRADE DOWN AGAIN, KAIJA ONE OF FEW RISERS.
newsitem.headline: SHARE TRADE DOWN AGAIN, KAIJA ONE OF FEW RISERS.

text.p: * Total volume came to 54,000 against 88,000 lats.
* Rietumu Bank index sheds 2.08 percent to 176.54.
* Most blue-chips retreated on Tuesday after the last session's slight gains, except for Kaija fish cannery.
* All official list stocks lost ground and Unibanka was ten santimes down to 3.50 lats.
* Kaija gained three santimes to 2.28 lats
Share volumes slipped to low levels again on Wednesday as shareholder meetings and approaching holidays kept a lid on activity, dealers said.
Total trade was just 54,000 lats versus yesterday's 88,000 lats and the Rietumu index slipped 2.08 percent to 176.54.
"The market was quite slow, people are just holding on to their stocks," said one trader, noting that any price movements were being made on small volumes.

Most leading shares dipped, with Riga Transport Fleet down 1.28 lats from 1.35 lats on low trade of 2,800 lats, Staburadze off 0.8 percent to 2.62 on 5,000 lats turnover and Unibanka down 10 santimes to 3.50 lats on trade of 8,500 lats.
Kaija was one of the few gainers, edging up three santimes to 2.28 lats on turnover of 6,900 lats.
The company earlier reported a first quarter profit of 80,980 lats although it did not provide comparatives.

Daugavpils Chain was most traded at 15,100 lats for a fall of six santimes to 2.25 lats as it holds today a new shareholder meeting to approve the issue of bonus shares. It has said it wants to issue 84 new shares for every 100 held.
Latvian Bridges was another stock that saw some volume. It was one of the few gainers, rising to 1.35 lats from 1.18 lats on trade of 6,000 lats. It recently announced a 1996 profit of 121,044 lats.
Valmiera Glassfibre was unchanged at 1.50 lats on turnover of 1,700 lats.
